On the right is the smaller triangle PNQ, vertex N has a double-arc angle marking matching H, vertex Q has a single-arc angle marking matching J; side QP is labeled 20, side NQ is labeled 12, side PN is labeled 8. Reasoning: From the angle markings, ∠H corresponds to ∠N, ∠J corresponds to ∠Q, therefore the remaining vertex K corresponds to P, and triangle HJK is similar to triangle NQP. The corresponding sides JK and QP have lengths 25 and 20 respectively, so the ratio from the large triangle to the small triangle is 25/20 = 5/4. Side HJ corresponds to side NQ, and NQ = 12, so HJ = 12 × 5/4 = 15.
